message.content:
I’m not sure there’s a single “most popular” security guard in New York—security services are usually organized by agencies or companies rather than individual guards. However, here are some practical ways to find a reputable, well‑reviewed security guard or security company in the NYC area: | What you’re looking for | How to find it | Tips & Resources | |-------------------------|----------------|------------------| | **Private security guard (individual)** | • Ask for referrals from friends, neighbors, or local businesses.
• Check local classified ads (e.g., Craigslist “Security” section).
• Search online directories like *Security Guard Jobs* or *Indeed* for “security guard” listings in NYC. | • Verify the guard’s credentials: check that they hold a valid NY State security guard license (issued by the NYS Department of State).
• Ask for references and check them.
• Look for any past disciplinary actions or complaints. | | **Security guard service from a company** | • Use online review sites: *Yelp*, *Google Maps*, *Angie’s List*, *HomeAdvisor*.
• Search “security guard services New York City” or “private security companies NYC.”
• Check the company’s website for client testimonials, case studies, and certifications. | • Look for companies that are members of the *National Association of Security Companies (NASCO)* or the *International Association of Professional Security Consultants (IAPSC).*
• Ask about their staff’s training (e.g., CPR, firearms, crowd control).
• Request a written contract that specifies duties, hours, insurance, and liability coverage. | | **Specialized security (e.g., event, executive protection, armed guard)** | • Narrow your search: “armed security guard NYC,” “event security NYC,” “executive protection NYC.”
• Contact local event venues or corporate security departments for recommendations. | • For armed guards, confirm they have a valid NYS *Armed Guard* license and that the company has a *Firearms Permit* (if required).
• Verify that the company carries *public liability* and *workers’ compensation* insurance. | ### Quick Steps to Get Started 1. **Define Your Needs** - Do you need a single guard for a home, office, or event? - Do you require armed or unarmed protection? - What hours and duration? 2. **Search & Shortlist** - Use Google or Yelp to pull up the top 5–10 providers. - Read at least 3–5 reviews for each. 3. **Verify Credentials** - For individuals: NYS Department of State’s *Security Guard License* database. - For companies: check their *Business License* and *Insurance* status. 4. **Interview & Ask Questions** - Inquire about training, experience, response times, and emergency protocols. - Request a copy of their standard operating procedures. 5. **Get a Quote & Contract** - Compare rates but don’t choose solely on price. - Ensure the contract covers scope of work, insurance, liability, and termination clauses. 6. **Trial Period** - If possible, start with a short-term contract to evaluate performance before committing long‑term. ### Useful Links - **NY State Department of State – Security Guard License Lookup** https://www.dos.ny.gov/licensing/sg.html - **National Association of Security Companies (NASCO)** https://www.nasco.org/ - **International Association of Professional Security Consultants (IAPSC)** https://www.iapsc.org/ - **Yelp – Security Guard Services NYC** https://www.yelp.com/search?find_desc=security+guard+services&find_loc=New+York%2C+NY - **Google Maps – Security Guard NYC** https://www.google.com/maps/search/security+guard+NYC/ If you let me know whether you’re after an individual guard or a company, and whether you need armed protection or just general surveillance, I can narrow down the options even further.
